title: Runtime evening catchup — Kai's scratchpad
content:
Evening catchup notes (quick brain dump)

Date: 2024-11-07
Who: Kai (catching up after on-call handoff)
Context: short, messy — capture next actions before I lose them. Trying to keep this lightweight so I can hand off tomorrow.

1) Quick summary
- Morning canary showed tail-latency blips on low-traffic hosts after KV-cache eviction rollout (~09:40 UTC). 95th spiked to ~1.2s for ~7 minutes, recovered after fallback to non-evicting profile.
- Ticket RINF-2371 created for spike; initial hypothesis: eviction jitter + small-batch partial unroll causing extra kernel memcpy in hot path.
- Related PR: runtime#482 (eviction backoff tweak) — rolled to canary at 08:30, reverted at 09:48.

2) Observations / logs to keep
- Sample from pod r-runtime-07 (09:41:12):
  - trace: token-gen loop stalled at KV::fetch_async -> kernel-stream-block (0.87s)
  - thread dump shows one worker with high CPU sys, others idle
- Metrics:
  - p95 (seq_len=64): baseline 220ms -> spike 1200ms
  - p99: baseline 480ms -> 1600ms (coincident)
  - evict-rate: 0.003/sec per shard during spike window

3) Repro attempts (local / staging)
- Tried synthetic load with kv-populated prefix sets (12k keys), sequence=64, batch=2. Could reproduce ~30% p95 increase but not full 5x.
- Added logging for memcpy counts in runtime profiler; saw extra memcpy when eviction path triggered mid-request.
- Repro note: needs interleaved small bursts + background eviction to hit. Single steady QPS doesn't reproduce reliably.

4) Hypotheses (ranked)
A) Eviction backoff logic causes short-lived cache miss storms at startup for shards, triggering repeated KV rebuilds and kernel copy churn.
B) Kernel scheduling interaction: eviction triggers large pinned-page memcpy which stalls the event loop on some cores (worker-affinity edge-case).
C) Memory allocator fragmentation (per-shard arena) increases memcpy cost in worst-case.

5) Short term actions (today / next 24h)
- (A1) Add stricter guard: when eviction rate > X within window, throttle eviction and mark shard as paused (quick PR, low-risk) — owner: Lina. Target: small PR by 11/08 morning.
- (A2) Add extra memcpy instrumentation to confirm path frequency (myself). Need microbench harness for pinned vs normal pages.
- (A3) Re-run canary with pinned->unpinned fallback disabled (saves one code path) to see impact. Ops: Ethan to schedule.
- (A4) Update incident note on RINF-2371 with reproducibility steps and logs (me).

6) Mid-term (next sprint)
- Rework eviction scheduling to be workload-aware (burst detection + smoothing). Design doc stub: confluence page linked above. Owner: Lina/Ethan pair.
- Investigate per-shard allocator improvements or reuse ring-buffers to reduce memcpy calls. Consider jemalloc arenas tuning.
- Add automatic canary rollback if p95 increases > 2x for 5m across hosts. (Product/console change)

7) Minor TODOs (one-off)
- grep logs for "KV::rebuild" across 2024-11-07 08:00-10:00 UTC and attach samples to ticket. (Assigned: Kai)
- Create small perf harness to simulate eviction+burst pattern (assigned: Kai).
- Add a short note in onboarding doc about "eviction can cause short tails" for SRE playbooks. (Assigned: Lina)

8) Scratch: commands + snippets (for my tomorrow run)
- kubectl logs -n runtime svc/runtime-canary -c runtime --since=20m | egrep "KV::|memcpy|evict" > /tmp/evict-sample.log
- ./tools/perf-harness --kv-size=12000 --seq=64 --pattern=bursty --batch=2 --workers=4
- small gdb hint: set follow-fork-mode child; bt full on blocked thread (for kernel stall)

9) Open questions / things to ask on handoff
- Did any other deploys overlap the canary window? (Product/infra)
- Is there a known kernel driver update on canary hosts last night? (infra)
- Should we lower default eviction aggressiveness in dedicated clusters by default? (ops + product)

10) Random ideas worth saving
- Instead of raw eviction, maintain a tiny LRU per-shard (hotset) that resists eviction for short windows; cheaper to maintain and avoids transient misses.
- Explore kernel-level memmove optimizations using numa-aware memcpy in the runtime (if pinned pages are the culprit).

11) End-of-day status
- Ticket created and linked, basic repro path logged.
- Lina to draft quick guard PR tomorrow.
- I will land instrumentation + perf harness and attach to ticket.

---
Notes to self: keep this doc minimal. If I don't finish the harness tonight, add a small README in /home/kai/work/evict-harness so someone else can pick it up.
